quotes.text: It was about 2002. We got guitars at Christmas and started playing together in my garage that summer.
Zane played the demo for 'Bet You Look Good On The Dancefloor' and we were in York, playing in front of four people.
It spread through [the fans] - it was more about them than us
We played this gig in this posh bar and it was one of the most incredible shows we ever did.
It was before we got signed and it got a bit crazy, people were jumping on settees at the side and bouncing off and crowd-surfing.

We made a playlist to play before [the set]. We just put a load of tunes on it and the last one was 'Imagine' by John Lennon. The crowd was ready for us to go on before that song dropped. We were standing behind the curtain doing what everyone else in the crowd was doing - singing along to Lennon. We kinda just went out and it was all easy after that.

I rarely listen to those old recordings... [and] as time goes on, the way you play the old tunes change more. We play the new ones pretty much how we recorded them. But the older tunes have changed a lot from how we recorded them.
Now it sometimes feels like they're cover versions... I say cover versions but obviously they're pretty good covers though. I think we're the best Arctic Monkeys covers band.

Every album we've done we've tried to move on in one way or another. The idea that we would stay the same seems impossible. I think knowing each other for so long and growing up together has spurred on that idea of wanting to shift.
It was an opportunity for us to do a new song and get back together for the first time in a couple of years and see if we could still do it
the band feels natural in the studio, which he described as their happy place
There's no conversations about it, but it's definitely something we love to do and we'll always do
This is a reason we'd do something. There's always going to be talk about it like, 'What does it mean for the band?' We want it to just be for these people and for this.

People are going between album cycles, off tour, they're not worried about that at the moment. Let's just come together and do this. Everyone made time in their schedule to do it. For us, everyone can agree that this is a good cause. No one's on the fence about whether we should help the kids or not.
see everyone and to fall back into the roles that we've always had with each other, musically and personally

Sometimes we might not see each other for six months, but when we do it's like we were never apart. That's just how we are with people, with each other. It translates musically as well. We just had a couple of days doing this and it felt like nothing had happened; no space between.
